problem: Prior visual navigation either builds costly global metric maps (SLAM / large global 3DGS) or relies on topological graphs and end-to-end foundation policies (ViNT, NoMaD) that lose geometric detail and degrade over long routes or under scene change.
motivation: Exploration videos are cheap to capture and define a traversable 'breadcrumb trail', but they lack 3D structure, so an agent that strays off the path cannot compute corrective actions. 3DGS built from pose-free videos can supply local geometry so a low-cost RGB-only robot without GPS or odometry can re-align with the trajectory.
key_idea: Represent an environment as a graph of small local 3DGS models built from one-pass videos, use VPR for coarse localization, then localize the robot in the local 3DGS via PnP-RANSAC and compute corrective actions toward the next demonstrated pose.
insight: Explicit geometric pose alignment against a local 3D model gives interpretable, drift-resistant control and beats zero-shot end-to-end policies, especially at long range (SR@12m 0.75 vs 0.42 for ViNT and 0.20 for NoMaD). The paper's own analysis shows the VPR module (YOPO-Loc) is the main bottleneck, with PnP failures the second, and that large scene changes (construction area) require the most human interventions. There is no ablation of the individual components.
method: YOPO-Campus dataset: about 4 h and 6 km of Jackal teleoperation over 35 campus trajectories with RGB-D, discrete actions (0.25 m, ±15°), GPS, compass and Wi-Fi FTM. Only RGB and actions are used by YOPO-Nav.
YOPO-Loc VPR: DINOv3 ViT-L backbone (last 2 layers unfrozen) with a BoQ aggregator and multi-similarity loss, trained on 6 GND campuses. Features are stored in a FAISS index for top-5 retrieval.

Local 3DGS graph: AnySplat feed-forward reconstruction in batches of about 55 frames at 448x336 gives 547 local 3DGS models with estimated poses, compressed to SOG format. Edges link consecutive frames within a video and, across videos, top-5 VPR candidates re-ranked by XFeat + LighterGlue matches (threshold 800). Dijkstra plans over the graph.

Metric scale recovery: render images at the known poses, segment the ground with SAM-2.1 from a single point click, fit a plane by RANSAC on the back-projected depth, and compare to the fixed 250 mm camera height to obtain a median scale factor.
Pose estimation: XFeat + LighterGlue matches between the live frame and the target frame's 3D points, then PnP-RANSAC (SQPnP) with Gauss-Newton refinement gives a 4x4 transform to the target pose.
Action generation: a simple non-holonomic kinematic model (rotate toward the goal, translate forward, rotate to match the target orientation) run for each frame along the planned path.
GUI with human-in-the-loop: discrete nudges of 0.25 m or 15° are allowed, after which the robot re-localizes with YOPO-Loc.

setting.backbone: DINOv3 ViT-L + BoQ VPR (fine-tuned) + AnySplat (frozen, pretrained) + SAM-2.1 + XFeat/LighterGlue; geometric PnP control, no learned policy
setting.training_data: VPR trained on GND (6 campuses, 55,317 train / 14,584 val images); the 3DGS graph is built from YOPO-Campus exploration videos; no policy training
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB only at test time (no GPS or odometry); depth comes from 3DGS
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: forward 0.25 m, turn ±15° (rotate-translate-rotate from the estimated transform)
setting.simulator: real world only (Clearpath Jackal on Rutgers Busch Campus)
setting.privileged: prior exploration video of the same environment (pre-exploration), the goal image, and the robot's fixed camera height of 250 mm; a human is allowed to intervene in the second experiment

numbers.eval_set_note: 3 exploration trajectories, 8-10 trials per trajectory per distance threshold, real robot in winter 2025
numbers.extra: uses exploration video of the same scene; no human intervention; distance thresholds 1.5-12 m
numbers.evidence: Table: image-goal success rate at different trajectory lengths (YOPO-Nav 1.0 / 0.94 / 0.81 / 0.75)

numbers.extra: human interventions allowed; path length 222.6 m; the other four paths are in the paper's table
numbers.evidence: Table: Straight Trajectory 222.6 m, 5 interventions, 17.6, 2280, 25.8 min (GT 908 actions, 15.8 min)

numbers_note: Success rates are printed as fractions (0.94 etc.), converted to percent. Only the Straight Trajectory row is shown for the intervention experiment; the other four paths (Varying Ground 7 interventions, Construction 15, Seasonal 8, Combined 3) are in the paper's table. Baselines ViNT and NoMaD are not listed.
results: On real-robot image-goal navigation, YOPO-Nav reaches SR 1.0/0.94/0.81/0.75 at 1.5/3/7/12 m versus ViNT 0.94/0.67/0.63/0.42 and NoMaD 0.83/0.53/0.53/0.20. It also completes 87-223 m paths with 3-15 human interventions. The comparison uses very small trial counts.
limitations: The scene representation is a static snapshot, so large scene changes (construction, heavy foliage) cause many interventions.
The VPR module is the main bottleneck, with jumpy or wrong matches at localization, plus occasional PnP failures and SAM ground-plane failures.

Evaluation is small (3 trajectories with 8-10 trials each, 1 trial per path in the intervention study), the baselines are zero-shot and not fine-tuned, and it needs a remote GPU and prior exploration video.
